expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: any old web instance, worker, scheduled job, or rollback binary that still reads it will fail after the migration

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: deploy the read-removal first, confirm all old processes are drained and no production queries reference the column, then schedule the drop as a separate contract release

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: DROP legacy_email destroys data. Restore requires a tested snapshot/PITR path; none was established here

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: A schema drop itself cannot be rolled back by redeploying code

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: Friday is fine only if: a named responder is available

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: make CI block destructive migrations unless an explicit approval gate confirms the prior read-removal release has already been deployed

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: CI and tests are useful detection, but they don't prove the rollout window or restore path

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: deploy the read-removal first [reversible] vs DROP legacy_email [irreversible]
